classifications.description: The payment-service is experiencing database connection timeouts and pool exhaustion, causing payment requests to fail.
evidence_lines: 2026-05-09T10:01:13.002Z ERROR [payment-service] trace_id=a81d11 order_id=ORD-78219 error_code=DB_CONN_TIMEOUT message="Database connection timed out while creating payment transaction"
2026-05-09T10:01:13.225Z WARN  [postgres-primary] db=payments active_connections=195 max_connections=200 wait_event=ClientRead message="connection pool near exhaustion"

2026-05-09T10:01:14.119Z ERROR [payment-service] trace_id=a81d11 exception=org.postgresql.util.PSQLException message="FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections"

classifications.description: The payment-service pod is crashing due to memory exhaustion and being OOM-killed.
evidence_lines: 2026-05-09T10:01:20.774Z WARN  [kubelet] namespace=prod pod=payment-service-7d9f84c9b6-rx2pm container=payment-service restart_count=3 reason=CrashLoopBackOff message="Back-off restarting failed container"
2026-05-09T10:01:22.553Z ERROR [payment-service] pod=payment-service-7d9f84c9b6-rx2pm exception=java.lang.OutOfMemoryError message="Java heap space"
2026-05-09T10:01:23.018Z WARN  [kubernetes] namespace=prod pod=payment-service-7d9f84c9b6-rx2pm event=OOMKilled message="Container killed due to memory limit exceeded"

classifications.description: PostgreSQL is also showing slow queries and lock waits, indicating database contention affecting payment processing.

2026-05-09T10:02:36.882Z ERROR [postgres-primary] db=payments lock_wait_ms=6032 blocked_query_hash=cd77aa blocking_pid=4421 message="transaction lock wait exceeded threshold"
2026-05-09T10:02:11.886Z ERROR [payment-service] trace_id=d33f81 order_id=ORD-78223 error_code=PAYMENT_INIT_FAILED message="Unable to initialize payment due to database connection failure"

2026-05-09T10:02:06.432Z WARN  [api-gateway] trace_id=c91f12 method=GET path=/api/v1/profile status=401 latency_ms=3102 upstream=auth-service message="authentication failed due to token validation timeout"

classifications.description: A recent deployment of payment-service version v2.8.4 appears to have triggered increased error rates and reduced availability.
evidence_lines: 2026-05-09T10:03:01.108Z INFO  [deployment-controller] namespace=prod deployment=payment-service version=v2.8.4 previous_version=v2.8.3 message="recent deployment detected within last 30 minutes"
2026-05-09T10:03:04.333Z WARN  [deployment-controller] deployment=payment-service version=v2.8.4 change_id=CHG-9182 message="error rate increased after deployment"
2026-05-09T10:04:08.551Z WARN  [kubernetes] namespace=prod deployment=payment-service available_replicas=1 desired_replicas=6 message="deployment availability below threshold"

per_issue.justification: This is in a production payment path, which is highly critical and directly revenue-impacting. The log shows connection pool exhaustion on the primary database and payment requests failing, with cascading impact to payment-service and api-gateway, indicating major user-facing degradation.

The payment-service is crashing repeatedly in prod due to OOMKilled and CrashLoopBackOff, so the service is not reliably available. Because this affects a critical payment service, the blast radius includes direct transaction failures and sustained availability loss, which is a major incident.

The production PostgreSQL instance is experiencing slow queries and lock waits that are already causing payment initialization failures. Since the affected service is payment-processing and the issue is persistent across multiple evidence lines, it represents significant user impact and SLA risk.

Authentication failures in prod affect a core platform dependency and can block users from accessing multiple downstream APIs. The repeated Redis latency and 401s through api-gateway show a broad, persistent user-facing impact rather than a rare edge case.

The deployment issue is in prod and has reduced availability of payment-service, but the service is still partially up with one available replica. This indicates a significant partial degradation with likely rollback or scaling workarounds available, rather than a full outage.

severity.overall_justification: The worst issues are the prod payment-service failures: database timeouts, OOM crashes, and reduced deployment availability are directly impacting payment processing. Because a critical revenue path is failing repeatedly with broad service impact, the incident is P1.

steps.action: On postgres-primary for db=payments, immediately relieve connection pressure by identifying long-lived sessions driving active_connections=195/200 and terminating nonessential sessions so reserved superuser slots remain available; evidence shows "connection pool near exhaustion" and "remaining connection slots are reserved".

Reduce payment-service database concurrency in prod by lowering the app-side pool size and request concurrency until postgres-primary active_connections drops below the warning threshold, because payment-service is failing on DB_CONN_TIMEOUT while the primary is at 195 of 200 connections.

Inspect the slow insert on table payment_transactions (slow_query_ms=8421, query_hash=ab91ff) and the lock wait exceeded threshold (lock_wait_ms=6032, blocked_query_hash=cd77aa, blocking_pid=4421) on postgres-primary; remove or resolve the blocking transaction and confirm the insert path is no longer waiting on locks.

Validate payment-service transaction retry behavior for trace_id=a81d11 and order_id=ORD-78219, then reprocess a failed payment only after postgres-primary reports healthy connection headroom and no active lock waits.

Investigate whether the connection pool exhaustion is caused by the recent payment_transactions slow inserts and lock contention by reviewing postgres-primary query plans and transaction isolation settings for the payment write path.

Stabilize payment-service in namespace=prod by temporarily increasing the pod memory limit for payment-service-7d9f84c9b6-rx2pm or scaling the deployment to replace the crashing pod, because kubelet reports CrashLoopBackOff and Kubernetes event OOMKilled.

Reduce JVM heap pressure in payment-service by setting the Java heap options below the container memory limit and restarting the workload, because the pod error is java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: "Java heap space".

Check the current resource requests/limits for deployment payment-service in prod and compare them with the crash pod payment-service-7d9f84c9b6-rx2pm to confirm whether the container memory limit is too low for peak transaction load.

Review payment-service application logs and heap usage patterns around 2026-05-09T10:01:22.553Z to identify any memory growth tied to payment transaction handling, object retention, or unbounded caches before restoring full traffic.

On postgres-primary, address the blocking transaction identified by blocking_pid=4421 and unblock the payment_transactions write path, since lock_wait_ms=6032 and payment-service is failing with PAYMENT_INIT_FAILED.
Reduce contention on table payment_transactions by pausing or rate-limiting the hottest payment writes from payment-service until slow_query_ms=8421 drops and new inserts stop timing out.
Inspect the slow insert query_hash=ab91ff on postgres-primary and determine whether missing indexes, dead tuples, or trigger overhead are causing the 8421 ms insert latency.
Retry the failed payment initialization for order_id=ORD-78223 only after postgres-primary reports no lock waits and payment-service can connect successfully without DB_CONN_TIMEOUT errors.

Restore Redis session lookup performance on redis-prod-01 by reducing latency for GET key=session:98281, because auth-service is failing token validation with reason="Redis session lookup timeout" and api-gateway is returning 401s.
Inspect redis-cache saturation, slow commands, and network reachability from auth-service to redis-prod-01 to determine why command latency reached 2740 ms for session:98281.

Temporarily increase auth-service tolerance for Redis lookup latency or enable a short-lived fallback path for token validation so api-gateway requests to /api/v1/profile stop failing while Redis is recovered.
Verify end-to-end token validation for trace_id=c91f12 after redis-cache recovers, then confirm api-gateway returns 200 instead of 401 for GET /api/v1/profile.

Roll back deployment payment-service version=v2.8.4 to previous_version=v2.8.3 in namespace=prod, because deployment-controller detected increased error rate after change_id=CHG-9182 and kubernetes reports only 1 of 6 replicas available.
Pause further rollout of payment-service v2.8.4 and verify that the remaining healthy replica is serving traffic while availability is below threshold at available_replicas=1 desired_replicas=6.
Compare logs and metrics between v2.8.3 and v2.8.4 for payment-service to identify the regression that caused the post-deploy error rate increase observed by deployment-controller.
Only after rollback or fix validation, re-enable the payment-service deployment in prod and confirm kubernetes restores available_replicas to 6/6 without increased errors.

summary: Payment-service is failing payments due to PostgreSQL connection timeouts and pool exhaustion (`DB_CONN_TIMEOUT`, `PSQLException: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved`), and it is also crashing with `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space` and `OOMKilled` in CrashLoopBackOff. Postgres-primary is under contention with `active_connections=195/200`, `slow_query_ms=8421`, and `lock_wait_ms=6032`, while auth-service and api-gateway are also returning 401s from Redis session lookup timeouts. Overall severity is P1, with immediate user impact on payment submission and authentication-dependent API access, and the recent payment-service v2.8.4 deployment has only 1/6 replicas available. The single most critical next step is to roll back payment-service from v2.8.4 to v2.8.3 and pause the rollout while relieving postgres-primary connection pressure.
